advisories.detail: The draft measures a28f7a23… (live at HEAD 9b06a2f). The frozen v14 contract pins the same path at b9819d6e… (D-105 HEAD) as its 'live digest at this authoring'. Two decisions have landed in between — C-D106 and C-D107 — so a reader comparing the draft's table to the subject's recordedInputs sees two different digests for one path with no stated reconciliation. A related instance sits inside the frozen subject: it describes component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v3 as the 'Current hand-authored catalog candidate', a time-indexed predicate that D-106's recording of corpus v6 has since overtaken.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The draft measures the file as its own input at draft time and makes no claim that its value equals the subject's pin, so nothing false is recorded. I verified independently that C-D106 and C-D107 disturb none of the eight properties the contract named at that pin, and that the file-08 pin has not moved at all — so the DR-120 row quoted verbatim in the contract is the row live today. The corpus-currency instance sits inside a frozen artifact already accepted at 0/0, and the dispatch directs me not to re-review the v14 contract beyond the draft's counts and digests, so it is reported to the coordinator rather than graded.

The now-frozen Codex v13 verdict (b1ce0753…, mode 0444) carries 0 blockers, exactly one SHOULD-FIX CPCV13-S1, and 0 advisories — nothing beyond CPCV13-S1. The condition is therefore not met, the v15 trigger does not fire, and the draft's unqualified recording is correct rather than merely unchallenged. The distinction here is that I closed the scope by measurement and it is empty. Recording an exhausted caveat as a defect would misdescribe the evidence.

authorityOfThisVerdict.whatConsentMeansHere: CONSENT is a statement about THIS DRAFT ONLY: at turn 1 of 3, zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX survive my adversarial measurement, so the draft is fit to proceed in the D-000 cycle. It does not adopt D-108, does not mark DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED, moves no register row, seals nothing, chooses no packager or toolchain, and authorizes nothing under docs/v2/implementation/.

coordinatorNote: The draft is accurate everywhere I could reach it, and it is precise in the two places this cycle has repeatedly been caught. It names the register path three times and refuses the coop/architecture substitution; it re-measured COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at the new HEAD instead of carrying D-107's value forward, which is the correction that took a full turn to land at D-104; and it transcribes Codex's ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES exactly rather than flattening it to ACCEPT. The advisory bookkeeping is the strongest part: three advisories from two reviewers, two of which describe records lost in the same ledger rotation and would merge under any careless reading. They are genuinely distinct — different locations, different missing records, and Codex's is sourced from a prior-generation Claude advisory rather than from Claude's v14 finding — so the draft's refusal to collapse them is correct and preserves all three. Two attacks were worth real work. The first was that Claude's ACCEPT is explicitly conditional on the then-unfrozen Codex v13 verdict; I opened that verdict and it carries exactly CPCV13-S1 and nothing else, so the residual is empty and no v15 is required on that ground. The second was that C-D106 and C-D107 have moved the COORD pin the frozen contract inherited; none of the eight named properties is disturbed, and the file-08 pin has not moved at all, so the DR-120 row quoted verbatim in the contract is the row live today. Both advisories travel as honesty work and neither is a gate. 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX: CONSENT.
